name: Haltija
body:
HALTIJA
CR 3

This small creature appears as a big-eared gnome with a cunning twinkle in its eyes and a rose-cheeked smile. Dressed in bright colors and wearing a crown of leaves or flowers, or a pointed hat, it watches from a hidden vantage point.

XP 800
N Small fey (haltija)
Init +7; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +15

DEFENSE

AC 17, touch 15, flat-footed 14 (+2 armor, +3 Dex, +1 dodge, +1 size)
hp 23 (5d6+5)
Fort +2, Ref +7, Will +7
Defensive Abilities domain warden; DR 5/cold iron

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., fly 30 ft.
Melee quarterstaff +2 (1d4-1)
Space 5 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks hearth’s revolt
Spell-like Abilities (CL 5th; concentration +8):

Constant—invisibility
At will—ethereal jaunt (self only)

Spells Prepared (CL 5th; concentration +8)

3rd—spike growth (DC 16)
2nd—flaming sphere (DC 15), gust of wind, lesser restoration
1st—entangle (DC 14), magic stone, obscuring mist, produce flame
0th—create water, detect magic, mending, purify food and drink

STATISTICS

Str 8, Dex 16, Con 12, Int 14, Wis 17, Cha 16
Base Atk +2; CMB +3; CMD 13
Feats Improved Initiative, Dodge, Skill Focus (Perception)
Skills Acrobatics +11, Bluff +11, Diplomacy +11, Disguise +11, Escape Artist +11, Perception +15, Sleight of Hand +11, Stealth +17
Languages Common, Sylvan
Gear leather armor, 2 potions of cure light wounds, potion of remove disease

Spells (Su)

A haltija casts spells as a 5th-level druid but can’t swap out prepared spells to cast summon spells.

ECOLOGY

Environment any.

Haltija are fey spirits tightly associated with a particular place or creature. Serving as protectors or stewards of what they oversee, they remain invisible most of the time but can reveal themselves if they wish. Their powers and domains can vary greatly but they do all share some commonalities such as requiring the connection to a domain in order to survive and the ability to become invisible or retreat into an extradimensional space that serves as their home as well as the ability to cast spells.

Most haltija are stewards of a small location, like a waterfall or forest glade, or a single creature or a small community from a family farm to a village, or even a pack of wolves or herd of reindeer. In turn, simple offerings of food or handicrafts are often left as a sign of the respect locals have for them.

The kotihaltija are house spirits that safeguard their chosen family and aid them in their labors where they can.

Rare haltija can be far more powerful, rising to be protectors of an entire forest or range of mountains.

Particularly powerful haltija can be seen as akin to minor deities and even attract worship. While they lack any true divine power and can’t grant spellcasting abilities, they may serve as intermediaries between mortals and true gods or wild spirits of nature.
